clauses.clause: Para. 1: property seized under the 26 listed executive orders or their amendments shall be returned to owners as soon as practicable, as determined by the holding officer with approval of the Director of Economic Stabilization
Para. 2: any listed order in conflict with this order is amended to the extent of the conflict

data_errors: The American Presidency Project transcription prints 'No. 8400 of Dec. 3, 1943' and 'No. 9508 of Dec. 27, 1945'; the Federal Register reads 9400 and Dec. 27, 1944.
The evidence slice's 'later_instruments_naming_it' lists earlier orders (1942-1945) that EO 9603 itself names. The direction is inverted: they are targets, not later instruments acting on EO 9603.

The OFR 1989 table 'acting' list includes EO 9320 and EO 9592A, which are not in the order's printed list of 26. EO 9320 is reached only through the words 'or amendments thereof' (as an amendment of EO 9108); the basis for 9592A was not checked.

gaps.what: Whether and when every plant, mine, facility and transportation system seized under the 26 listed orders was returned to its owner. Without it, the return command cannot be marked ended by performance.
gaps.where_to_look: Federal Register 1945-1946 termination-of-possession notices by the War and Navy Departments, Office of Defense Transportation, Interior (Solid Fuels/Coal Mines Administration) and Petroleum Administration for War; J. L. Blackman, Presidential Seizure in Labor Disputes (1967), appendix tables of seizures and release dates

gaps.what: Any later instrument expressly revoking or superseding EO 9603. None appears in the slice or the OFR table entry.
gaps.where_to_look: OFR Codification of Presidential Proclamations and Executive Orders disposition tables; the 3 CFR 1943-1948 compilation tables

gaps.what: Whether the lapse of the War Labor Disputes Act seizure power (a general statute that does not name the order) should count as ending the return command. Recorded as a candidate only; the Act's termination provision was not read.
gaps.where_to_look: War Labor Disputes Act, 57 Stat. 163, termination provision; Proclamation 2714 of 31 December 1946

moves.note: Status OPEN with named gap: no express revocation found, no current source, and performance of the return command is unsourced.
Both clauses have a state: the amendment clause is spent on issue; the return command is open with the gap named.
Needs proof that every property seized under the 26 listed orders was returned (agency termination notices or a print compilation); not in the held files and not found in one web search.

propositions.claim: EO 9603 is printed in the Federal Register of 28 August 1945 at 10 FR 10960, signed 25 August 1945.
propositions.quote: EXECUTIVE ORDER 9603 Termination of P ossession of C ertain Property T aken by the G overnment

propositions.claim: The order commands return of all property seized under the listed orders or their amendments.
propositions.quote: shall be returned to the owners thereof as soon as practicable

propositions.claim: Timing of each return is left to the holding officer with approval of the Director of Economic Stabilization, so return is not completed by the order itself.
propositions.quote: in each case by the officer by whom the property in question is held and operated for the government, with the approval of the Director of Economic Stabiliza­tion

propositions.claim: The order itself amends the listed orders to the extent of conflict, a one-time act completed on issue.
propositions.quote: Any of the above-listed orders in con­flict with this order is hereby amended to the extent of such conflict.

propositions.claim: The order is dated 25 August 1945 and was filed 27 August 1945.

The order rests on section 9 of the Selective Training and Service Act as amended by the War Labor Disputes Act. Expiry of that statutory seizure power is only a candidate ending, since no instrument naming EO 9603 was read.
propositions.quote: including section 9 of the Selective Training and Service Act of 1940 (54 Stat. 892) as amended by the War Labor Disputes Act (57 Stat. 163)

propositions.claim: The OFR 1989 disposition table records only that EO 9603 terminates provisions of other orders; the slice shows no revocation or supersession of EO 9603 itself.

Read the held American Presidency Project transcription and compared its list with the Federal Register printing

Web search (standard): "Executive Order 9603" 1945 seized plants returned to owners, termination of possession, War Labor Disputes Act. It returned only texts of the order and of the listed seizure orders, with no evidence of returns.

review.conclusion_reason: OPEN is supported because the return command requires performance and no evidence establishes completion for all covered property. Paragraph 2 performs its amendment on August 25, 1945. Formal status is supported only as no express ending found in the reviewed evidence. The basis should identify the unproved performance required by rule (e), rather than simply 'none'.
review.stop_code_verdict: wrong (NOT_FOUND fits the supplied record: completion evidence is missing, but no offline barrier is demonstrated)
review.suspected_defect: The first gap's OFFLINE label is unsupported: neither the result nor the slice documents an access failure or establishes that the required return records are available only offline.

verdicts.reason: Held Federal Register text identifies EO 9603, page 10960, August 28, 1945, and the August 25 signature date.
The original commands that all property seized under the 26 listed orders 'or amendments thereof' 'shall be returned to the owners thereof as soon as practicable'.

The original assigns the determination in each case to the holding officer, with the Director of Economic Stabilization's approval. It directs future performance rather than itself returning possession.
The original says conflicting listed orders are 'hereby amended to the extent of such conflict'. That textual amendment occurs on issue; EO 9603 is not an amendment-only order.
The signature and filing block confirms August 25, 1945, and August 27, 1945, at 10:25 a.m.

The statutory-authority quotation matches the original. Treating statutory expiry only as an unverified candidate is consistent with the project rules; neither expiry nor its effect on this command is established here.

The cited evidence-slice field describes termination of provisions of other orders and supplies no express ending of EO 9603. This confirms the slice's contents, not an independently inspected OFR table or an exhaustive absence of later instruments.

stop_code_verdict: wrong (NOT_FOUND fits the supplied record: completion evidence is missing, but no offline barrier is demonstrated)
